discovery: Time reversal and wavefront shaping of waves for focusing and imaging through complex, multiply scattering media

nominees.name: Mathias Fink
nominees.affiliation: Institut Langevin, ESPCI Paris - PSL, France

subfield: Wave physics / optics of complex media
motivation: Multiple scattering was long regarded as the ultimate barrier to focusing and imaging with waves. Mathias Fink showed with time-reversal mirrors that scattering can instead be exploited: waves re-emitted in time-reversed form refocus through disordered media, with resolution beyond the aperture limit, founding a new paradigm in acoustics and electromagnetism. In 2007 Vellekoop and Mosk carried this into optics, demonstrating that by shaping the incident wavefront with a spatial light modulator, light can be focused through fully opaque materials, with enhancement governed by the number of controlled mesoscopic channels. Together these works turned disorder from a limitation into a resource. They launched the field of wavefront shaping, which includes transmission-matrix measurement, open-channel physics, imaging through tissue and fibres, deep-brain microscopy, optical computing and high-dimensional quantum optics. The work combines fundamental mesoscopic wave physics with broad practical impact.
